questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Natural Logarithm Function
questions.worked_solution:
The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x)=\frac{1}{x}
$$

We apply our formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2eln⁡x) \\  & =2e\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x) \\  & =2e\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =\frac{2e}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $y=2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x) \\  & =2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =2e\cdot {1}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{1} \\  & =2e-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base
questions.worked_solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{xln⁡a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{e}^{x}+3{log}_{5}⁡x) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{5}⁡x) \\  & =-{e}^{x}+3\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡(5)} \\  & =-{e}^{x}+\frac{3}{xln⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $y=2{x}^{3}-5{log}_{3}⁡x,$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=2$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}-5{log}_{3}⁡x) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{3}⁡x) \\  & =2\cdot 3{x}^{2}-5\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡3} \\  & =6{x}^{2}-\frac{5}{xln⁡3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(6{x}^{2}-\frac{5}{xln⁡3})|}_{x=2} \\  & =6(2)^{2}-\frac{5}{2ln⁡3} \\  & =24-\frac{5}{2ln⁡3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $y=4{e}^{x}-3{log}_{2}⁡x+7,$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=3$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{x}-3{log}_{2}⁡x+7) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{2}⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7) \\  & =4{e}^{x}-3\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡2}+0 \\  & =4{e}^{x}-\frac{3}{xln⁡2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(4{e}^{x}-\frac{3}{xln⁡2})|}_{x=3} \\  & =4{e}^{3}-\frac{3}{3\cdot ln⁡2} \\  & =4{e}^{3}-\frac{1}{ln⁡2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent Line of a Logarithmic Function at a Point
questions.problem: Given that $y=3x-5+8{log}_{2}⁡x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=\frac{1}{ln⁡2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-5+8{log}_{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-5)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8{log}_{2}⁡x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5)+8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{2}⁡x) \\  & =3-0+8\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡2} \\  & =3+\frac{8}{xln⁡2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=\frac{1}{ln⁡2}$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1/ln⁡2} & ={(3+\frac{8}{xln⁡2})|}_{x=1/ln⁡2} \\  & =3+\frac{8}{(\frac{1}{ln⁡2}\cdot ln⁡2)} \\  & =3+8 \\  & =11\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $y=6{log}_{2}⁡x+4{x}^{2}-3x,$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{log}_{2}⁡x+4{x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{2}⁡x)+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡2}+4\cdot 2x-3 \\  & =\frac{6}{xln⁡2}+8x-3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{6}{xln⁡2}+8x-3)|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{6}{1\cdot ln⁡2}+8(1)-3 \\  & =\frac{6}{ln⁡2}+5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $y=3ln⁡x+2{x}^{2}-5x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3ln⁡x+2{x}^{2}-5x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3ln⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{x}+4x-5 \\  & =\frac{3}{x}+4x-5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{3}{x}+4x-5)|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{1}+4\cdot 1-5 \\  & =3+4-5 \\  & =2\,.\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$

$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent Line of a Logarithmic Function at a Point
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $y= \log_4 x + \ln x$,  find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}
		&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( \log_4 x + \ln x \right)\
		&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\log_4 x) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\ln x )\
		&= \dfrac{1}{x\ln 4} + \dfrac{1}{x}.
}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{1}{xln⁡4}+\frac{1}{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{ln⁡4}+1.\end{aligned}
$$
